U6-05511: I sat with a group of Quraysh, and a man came—coarse in hair, clothing, and appearance—until he stood over them, greeted them with salām, and said: "Give glad tidings to those who hoard wealth of a heated stone that will be heated in the fire of Hell and then placed on the nipple of the breast of one of them until it comes out from the soft part of his shoulder blade, and it will be placed on the soft part of his shoulder blade until it comes out from the nipple of his breast, shaking and quivering." Then he turned away and sat by a pillar. I followed him and sat with him, not knowing who he was. I said to him, "I see that the people disliked what you said." He said, "They understand nothing. My beloved friend said to me—" I said, "Who is your beloved friend?" He said, "The Prophet ﷺ. He said: 'O Abū Dharr, do you see Uhud?' I looked at the sun to see how much of the day remained, thinking that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was going to send me on some errand of his, and I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'I would not like to have gold the like of Uhud that I would spend all of it, except three dinars.'" And these people do not understand; they only accumulate the things of this world. No, by Allah, I will not ask them for anything of this world, nor seek religious rulings from them, until I meet Allah.
U6-05517: "Two gardens." Al-Layth said: Jaʿfar narrated to me from Ibn Hurmuz: I heard Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ: "Two gardens."
U6-05543: I came to Shaybah, and Qabīṣah narrated to us: Sufyān narrated to us, from Wāṣil, from Abū Wāʾil, who said: I sat with Shaybah on the seat in the Kaʿbah, and he said: ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, sat in this very seat and said: "I had resolved not to leave in it any yellow [gold] or white [silver] without distributing it." I said, "Your two companions did not do that." He said, "They are the two men whom I follow."
U6-05551: I met Anas. Ismāʿīl ibn Abān narrated to me: Abū Bakr narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, who said: I went out to Minā on the Day of Tarwiyah and met Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, going on a donkey. I said, "Where did the Prophet ﷺ pray the Ẓuhr prayer on this day?" He said, "Look where your rulers pray, and pray there."
U6-05553: I was looking for a camel of mine. Musaddad narrated to us: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, who heard Muḥammad ibn Jubayr, from his father Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, who said: I lost a camel of mine and went out to look for it on the Day of ʿArafah. I saw the Prophet ﷺ standing at ʿArafah, and I said, "By Allah, this man is one of the Ḥums, so what is he doing here?"
U6-05684: "The ʿumrā is permissible." ʿAṭāʾ said: Jābir narrated to me, from the Prophet ﷺ, something similar.
U6-05720: I asked Anas. ʿAmr ibn Zurārah narrated to us: Ziyād narrated to us: Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl narrated to me, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: My uncle Anas ibn al-Naḍr was absent from the battle of Badr and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I was absent from the first battle you fought against the polytheists. If Allah lets me witness a battle against the polytheists, Allah will surely see what I do." On the day of Uḥud, when the Muslims were routed, he said, "O Allah, I apologize to You for what these have done"—meaning his companions—"and I declare myself free of what these have done"—meaning the polytheists. Then he advanced, and Saʿd ibn Muʿādh met him. He said, "O Saʿd ibn Muʿādh, Paradise! By the Lord of al-Naḍr, I can smell its fragrance coming from beyond Uḥud." Saʿd said, "O Messenger of Allah, I was not able to do what he did." Anas said: We found on him more than eighty wounds from the sword, spear thrusts, or arrows. We found that he had been killed and the polytheists had mutilated him, and no one recognized him except his sister, by his fingertips. Anas said: We used to think that this verse was revealed about him and those like him: "Among the believers are men who were true to what they pledged to Allah" to the end of the verse. And he said: His sister, who was called al-Rubayyiʿ, broke the front tooth of a woman, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered retaliation. Anas ibn al-Naḍr said, "O Messenger of Allah, by the One who sent you with the truth, her tooth will not be broken." So they accepted compensation and gave up retaliation. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Among the servants of Allah are those who, if they swore an oath by Allah, He would fulfill it for them."
U6-05887: "He taught him the Book." Mūsā narrated to us: Wuhayb narrated to us, from Khālid, similarly. And wisdom is attaining what is correct, other than prophethood.
U6-06029: O Messenger of Allah—Muḥammad ibn Muqātil narrated to us: ʿAbdullāh informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: When we returned from Ḥunayn, ʿUmar asked the Prophet ﷺ about a vow he had made during the Jāhiliyyah (pre-Islamic period) to observe iʿtikāf (seclusion in the mosque), and the Prophet ﷺ commanded him to fulfil it. Some of them said: Ḥammād [narrated] from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar. It was also narrated by Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim and Ḥammād ibn Salamah, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet ﷺ.
U6-06067: The Prophet ﷺ—ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to me: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us; Hishām said: he narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, from ʿUbaydah, from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said on the day of the Trench: "They kept us from the middle prayer until the sun set. May Allah fill their graves and their houses—or their bellies (Yaḥyā was unsure)—with fire."
U6-06075: It is a firm, binding ruling and is not abrogated. Saʿīd corroborated it from Ibn ʿAbbās.
U6-06218: With a boy there is an ʿaqīqah (birth sacrifice). Ḥajjāj said: Ḥammād narrated to us: Ayyūb, Qatādah, Hishām and Ḥabīb informed us, from Ibn Sīrīn, from Salmān, from the Prophet ﷺ.
U6-06275: The sun was eclipsed on the day Ibrāhīm died. Abū Bakrah narrated it from the Prophet ﷺ.
U6-06281: That he came to Syria. And Abū al-Walīd narrated to us: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Mughīrah, from Ibrāhīm, who said: ʿAlqamah went to Syria, came to the mosque, and prayed two rakʿahs. He said: "O Allah, grant me a companion to sit with." Then he sat with Abū al-Dardāʾ, who said: "Where are you from?" He said: "From the people of Kufa." He said: "Is there not among you the keeper of the secret that no one else knew," meaning Ḥudhayfah, "Is there not among you," or "Was there not among you, the one whom Allah protected from the Devil on the tongue of His Messenger ﷺ," meaning ʿAmmār, "and is there not among you the keeper of the siwāk and the cushion," meaning Ibn Masʿūd? "How did ʿAbdullāh recite {By the night when it covers}?" He said: "{And the male and the female}." He said: "These people kept on until they almost made me doubt, though I heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
U6-06340: "The major sins." And ʿAmr narrated to us: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Bakr, from Anas ibn Mālik, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The greatest of the major sins are associating partners with Allah, killing a person, disobedience to parents, and false speech," or he said, "and false testimony."
U6-06347: I said to ʿAlī—and Ṣadaqah ibn al-Faḍl narrated to us: Ibn ʿUyaynah informed us: Muṭarrif narrated to us: I heard al-Shaʿbī narrating, saying: I heard Abū Juḥayfah say: I asked ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him: "Do you have anything [of revelation] that is not in the Qurʾān?" Ibn ʿUyaynah once said: "that the people do not have?" He said: "By the One who split the grain and created the soul, we have nothing except what is in the Qurʾān, apart from the understanding that a man is given of His Book, and what is in this sheet." I said: "And what is in the sheet?" He said: "The blood-money, the ransoming of captives, and that a Muslim is not to be killed for a disbeliever."
U6-06398: ʿAṭāʾ [said]: Jābir said—Abū ʿAbdillāh said: And Muḥammad ibn Bakr said: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us: ʿAṭāʾ informed me: I heard Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh, among some people with him, say: We, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, entered the state of iḥrām for Hajj alone, with no ʿUmrah along with it. ʿAṭāʾ said: Jābir said: The Prophet ﷺ arrived on the morning of the fourth of Dhū al-Ḥijjah. When we arrived, the Prophet ﷺ commanded us to leave iḥrām and said: "Leave iḥrām and be intimate with women." ʿAṭāʾ said: Jābir said: He did not make it obligatory on them, but he made it lawful for them. Then it reached him that we were saying: "When there are only five days between us and ʿArafah, he commands us to become lawful to our wives, so we would come to ʿArafah with our private parts dripping with pre-seminal fluid." He said: And Jābir gestured with his hand like this and moved it. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up and said: "You know that I am the most God-fearing of you, the most truthful of you, and the most dutiful of you. Were it not for my sacrificial animal, I would have left iḥrām as you do. So leave iḥrām, for if I had known beforehand what I came to know afterward, I would not have brought the sacrificial animal." So we left iḥrām, and we listened and obeyed.
U6-06401: "[People] will keep being thrown into the Fire". And Khalīfah said to me: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us: Saʿīd narrated to us from Qatādah, from Anas. And from Muʿtamir: I heard my father, from Qatādah, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "It will keep being thrown into, and it will say, 'Is there any more?' until the Lord of the worlds places His foot in it, and its parts draw together, and it says, 'Enough, enough, by Your might and Your generosity.' And Paradise will continue to have surplus room until Allah creates a new creation for it and settles them in the surplus of Paradise."
U6-06408: ...and al-Aʿraj. And Ismāʿīl narrated to us: my brother narrated to me, from Sulaymān, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAtīq, from Ibn Shihāb, from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, that Abū Hurayrah said: A man from the Muslims and a man from the Jews insulted each other. The Muslim said, in an oath he swore by, "By the One who chose Muḥammad over all the worlds!" The Jew said, "By the One who chose Moses over all the worlds!" At that, the Muslim raised his hand and slapped the Jew. The Jew went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him what had happened between him and the Muslim. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Do not give me preference over Moses, for people will fall unconscious on the Day of Resurrection, and I will be the first to recover, and there will be Moses holding on to a side of the Throne. I do not know whether he was among those who fell unconscious and recovered before me, or whether he was among those whom Allah exempted."
U6-06605: ʿAmr said: He traced it back [to the Prophet]; and Abū Bakr said: He attributed it directly [to the Prophet].
U6-06714: The wife of ʿAbdullāh. He said: I mentioned it to Ibrāhīm, and he narrated to me from Abū ʿUbaydah, from ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith, from Zaynab, the wife of ʿAbdullāh, exactly the same. She said: I was in the mosque and the Prophet ﷺ saw me and said: "Give charity, even from your jewelry." And he related the hadith like the hadith of Abū al-Aḥwaṣ.
U6-06748: May Allah be pleased with him. And Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd narrated to us: Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Qatādah and ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Ṣuhayb, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Eat the pre-dawn meal, for in the pre-dawn meal there is blessing."
U6-06752: May Allah be pleased with her. And Shujāʿ ibn Makhlad narrated to us: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Zāʾidah narrated to us: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Muslim, from Masrūq, from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to kiss while fasting and used to have physical contact [with his wives] while fasting, but he had the greatest control over his desire among you.
U6-06761: May Allah be pleased with him. And Abū Bakr ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to me, and the wording is his: Bahz narrated to us: Ḥammād narrated to us: Thābit narrated to us, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would fast until it was said, "He has fasted, he has fasted," and he would go without fasting until it was said, "He has stopped fasting, he has stopped fasting."
U6-06777: May Allah be pleased with them both. And Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, and the wording is his: Hushaym informed us, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, that a man who was in a state of iḥrām with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was thrown by his camel, which broke his neck, and he died. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Wash him with water and lote-tree leaves, shroud him in his two garments, do not touch him with perfume, and do not cover his head, for he will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection reciting the talbiyah."
U6-06781: May Allah be pleased with her. And Ibn Abī ʿUmar narrated it to us: Sufyān narrated to us, from Yaḥyā, with this chain of narration, the same.
U6-06830: Anas. And Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, and the wording is his: Hushaym informed us, from Ḥumayd, from Thābit al-Bunānī, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a man driving a sacrificial camel and said: "Ride it." He said, "It is a sacrificial camel." He said: "Ride it," two or three times.
U6-07008: He dictated it to us. (Another chain:) ʿAbdullāh ibn Hāshim narrated to me, the wording being his: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, meaning Ibn Mahdī, narrated to me: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAlqamah ibn Marthad, from Sulaymān ibn Buraydah, from his father, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed a commander over an army or a detachment, he would advise him personally to fear Allah and to treat the Muslims with him well. Then he said: "Fight in the name of Allah, in the cause of Allah. Fight those who disbelieve in Allah. Fight, but do not steal from the spoils, do not betray, do not mutilate, and do not kill a child. When you meet your enemy from among the polytheists, call them to three options, or three qualities. Whichever of them they respond to, accept it from them and hold back from them. Then call them to Islam; if they respond to you, accept it from them and hold back from them. Then call them to move from their land to the land of the Muhājirūn, and inform them that if they do so, they will have what the Muhājirūn have and owe what the Muhājirūn owe. If they refuse to move from it, inform them that they will be like the Bedouin Muslims: the ruling of Allah that applies to the believers will apply to them, but they will have no share in the war booty or the fayʾ unless they strive together with the Muslims. If they refuse, ask them for the jizyah; if they respond to you, accept it from them and hold back from them. If they refuse, seek help from Allah and fight them. When you besiege the people of a fortress and they want you to grant them the protection of Allah and the protection of His Prophet, do not grant them the protection of Allah or the protection of His Prophet, but grant them your own protection and the protection of your Companions, for if you break your own pledges and the pledges of your Companions, that is lighter than breaking the pledge of Allah and the pledge of His Messenger. And when you besiege the people of a fortress and they want you to let them surrender according to the judgment of Allah, do not let them surrender according to the judgment of Allah, but let them surrender according to your own judgment, for you do not know whether you will arrive at the judgment of Allah concerning them or not." ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: This is it, or something like it. Isḥāq added at the end of his narration, from Yaḥyā ibn Ādam, who said: I mentioned this ḥadīth to Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān. Yaḥyā said: meaning that ʿAlqamah was telling it to Ibn Ḥayyān. He said: Muslim ibn Hayṣam narrated to me, from al-Nuʿmān ibn Muqarrin, from the Prophet ﷺ, something similar.
U6-07053: Like the ḥadīth of al-Layth from Nāfiʿ. Abū Isḥāq said: Al-Ḥasan ibn Bishr narrated to us: ʿAbdullāh ibn Numayr narrated to us, from ʿUbaydullāh, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, with this, like the ḥadīth of al-Layth from Nāfiʿ.
U6-07598: I said to al-Miqdād... and he mentioned its meaning. Abū Dāwūd said: Al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Faḍālah and a group, as well as al-Thawrī and Ibn ʿUyaynah, narrated it from Hishām, from his father, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib. Ibn Isḥāq narrated it from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from al-Miqdād, from the Prophet ﷺ, and he did not mention "his testicles."
U6-07714: Like the ḥadīth of Wuhayb. Ismāʿīl said: I narrated it to Ayyūb, and he said: "Except for the iqāmah."
U6-08068: It does not mention wheat. Abū Dāwūd said: Muʿāwiyah ibn Hishām mentioned in this ḥadīth, from al-Thawrī, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿIyāḍ, from Abū Saʿīd, "half a ṣāʿ of wheat." That is an error on the part of Muʿāwiyah ibn Hishām or of someone who narrated it from him.
U6-08334: "The one who performs cupping and the one who has it done have broken their fast." Shaybān said: Abū Qilābah informed me that Abū Asmāʾ al-Raḥabī narrated to him that Thawbān, the freed slave of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, informed him that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [say this].
U6-08337: "The one who performs cupping and the one who has it done have broken their fast." Abū Dāwūd said: Ibn Thawbān narrated it from his father, from Makḥūl, with his chain, the same.
U6-08425: With the chain of ʿAbbād and its meaning. Abū Dāwūd said: Maʿmar, Shuʿayb and ʿUqayl narrated it from al-Zuhrī, from men of knowledge, and this is more authentic in our view.
U6-08813: And he mentioned its meaning. Abū Dāwūd said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd looked at al-Ḥārith ibn ʿUmayr and said: This is one of the trustworthy students of Ayyūb.
U6-09031: There is no harm in qarāmil (hair extensions of wool or similar material). Abū Dāwūd said: It seems he held that what is prohibited is [the use of] women's [natural] hair. Abū Dāwūd said: Aḥmad used to say: There is no harm in qarāmil.
U6-09190: The ghurrah is five hundred dirhams. Abū Dāwūd said: Rabīʿah said: The ghurrah is fifty dinars.
U6-09193: "The foot is without liability." Abū Dāwūd said: [It means] an animal striking with its foot while its owner is riding it.
U6-09288: "The best gatherings are the most spacious of them." Abū Dāwūd said: He is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr ibn Abī ʿAmrah al-Anṣārī.
U6-09654: "Here I am for ʿUmrah and Hajj." He said: And on this topic there are narrations from ʿUmar and ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn.
U6-09870: "Every intoxicant is forbidden." He said: On this topic there are also narrations from ʿUmar, ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd, Anas, Abū Saʿīd, Abū Mūsā, al-Ashajj al-ʿAṣarī, Daylam, Maymūnah, Ibn ʿAbbās, Qays ibn Saʿd, an-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr, Muʿāwiyah, Wāʾil ibn Ḥujr, Qurrah al-Muzanī, ʿAbdullāh ibn Mughaffal, Umm Salamah, Buraydah, Abū Hurayrah and ʿĀʾishah.
U6-10512: Similar to this. Aḥmad ibn Khālid al-Khallāl narrated it to us: Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq as-Sīlaḥānī narrated to us: al-Layth ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Jazʾ, who said: The laughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was never anything but a smile.
U6-11628: "Drink, but do not become intoxicated." Abū ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān said: This too is not authentic, and we do not know who this Qarṣāfah is. What is well known from ʿĀʾishah is contrary to what Qarṣāfah narrated from her.
